decision: Candidate analogy only; check whether an engineering entity and a configured computing whole have matching identity conditions.
Specification aggregates design requirements; matching a specific local description requires decomposition and scope.
Function denotes what an artifact is supposed to do. Do not collapse intended function and actual disposition.
A characteristic of a Part and a description artifact are not established as the same category.
Cloning a template graph does not establish identity of a configured bearer whole.
Information-lifecycle records may be related, but no evidence or result class equivalence is established.
Shared terminology is a correspondence lead, not proof of matching identity, typing or cardinality.

decision: Compare intended description and governance before any import or identity merge.
Source copy is a complex disposition. OntoSPK capability is a disposition and realization is its bearer whole; explicit bearer analysis is needed.
The local specification is an information artifact; do not map it to a stakeholder intention.
A general program execution is broader than a concluded test attempt; a setup-only abort may lack target participation.
Only evidenced exercised-code attempts are candidates; manual procedures and report documentation do not match code or creation automatically.
